Subject: Plan transition: downgrading from Tier+ to Core — minimum guarantees and feature portability

Hi Neha,

Quick one from our side as we look to tighten spend for Q1: we need clarity on what would change if we move Catalyst Health from Tier+ to Core. Specific asks:
- Is there a minimum throughput guarantee (RPS or token SLO) for Core vs Tier+?
- If we downgrade, can we keep the same feature set (especially embeddings storage and the custom reranker) or will those be removed?
- Would we be eligible for prorated credits / a transitional discount for the remainder of our current term?
- Timeline — how long to switch with minimal risk to production?

We have a renewal call next week and want to present concrete options. Can you propose a safe downgrade path that doesn’t break our workflows?

Thanks,
Liam

Catalyst Health

Subject: Re: Plan transition: downgrading from Tier+ to Core — minimum guarantees and feature portability

Hi team — looping you in. Summary of asks from Catalyst above. My initial read: this is a classic packaging question where we can offer a staged downgrade with a small concession to keep them from churn. Two practical paths to propose (I'll draft language to send to Catalyst once we agree):

Option A — Staged downgrade (recommended)
- 4-week grace period on current Tier+ throughput and KV/embedding retention.
- During the grace period we run them on Core with a temporary burst pool (paid add-on) to preserve spike capacity.
- After 4 weeks, Core's standard SLO applies; embeddings will be retained for 90 days in Core storage; beyond that they'd move to archived blob.
- Prorated credits equal to unused Tier+ tokens for the month of transition.

Option B — Immediate swap with concession
- Immediate downgrade to Core with a one-time 15% discount for 3 months to ease migration.
- Feature gating for the reranker: we keep a read-only copy of the model weights and embeddings for 60 days.

Practical notes:
- We should avoid promising multi-month retention of live KV cache unless they sign up for Dedicated or an add-on.
- I'll attach a draft pricing spreadsheet with the concession math and an SOW stub showing timelines (pricing-table.xlsx).

Ben: can you confirm estimated cost of a 1-month burst pool and how we would bill it?
Priyom: will need legal/ops language for the 15% concession if we go that route.
Lauren: can you confirm whether we can approve a one-time concession up to 20% in AMER deals?

I can draft the external note for Catalyst once we settle on the path.

Thanks,
Neha

Subject: Re: Plan transition: downgrading from Tier+ to Core — minimum guarantees and feature portability

Quick reply — technical + billing ops:

- 1-month burst pool (NVIDIA-backed) to cover peak traffic is roughly $4,250 incremental for Catalyst's profile (based on their 95th percentile). We can charge core+burst as a monthly line item, billed pro rata.
- Embeddings: we can keep them live for 90 days on Core storage, then archive. If they need unlimited retention, they'd have to commit to Dedicated or add the "Archive Retention" addon.
- Reranker: we can run the reranker as a hosted managed job for 60 days post-downgrade; beyond that we can provide a snapshot export.

From a delivery standpoint, staged downgrade (Option A) is lower risk and easier to justify as a migration service.

Attn Neha: I'll add the burst-line to the pricing-table.xlsx and push a short cost note.

Ben

Also: make the SOW explicit that embeddings retention beyond 90 days requires an add-on or Dedicated. Keep the language non-committal for persistence beyond that.

Hi Liam / Catalyst team — thanks for the patience while we pulled internal approvals. Here's a concise path we recommend and the concrete next steps so you can present this in your renewal conversation: 

Agreed path (Option A — staged downgrade, recommended):
- 4-week grace period where we run Catalyst on Core + a 1-month burst pool (paid add-on) to preserve peak capacity. Estimated burst cost: $4,250 (pro-rated).
- Embeddings and reranker: live retention on Core for 90 days post-downgrade. Reranker will be available as a managed job for 60 days; we will provide an export/snapshot after that window.
- Prorated credit: we will issue a credit for unused Tier+ token commitments for the month of transition.
- Concession: Redwood will apply a one-time 15% concession for 3 months to ease the migration (approved by Revenue Ops).

Attachments: Catalyst_SOW_v2.pdf (timeline + migration tasks), pricing-table.xlsx (breakdown including burst-add and concession). DocuSign for the amendment: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123

Next steps:
1) Review SOW attached and confirm the migration window you'd prefer (we suggest week of Nov 29).
2) If you agree, sign the amendment via DocuSign and we'll schedule a kickoff with Ben and our PM for the migration plan.
3) We will provision the burst pool on receipt of the signed amendment and apply the 15% concession to your next three invoices.

If Catalyst wants a steeper discount or longer retention windows we should discuss Dedicated or an Archive Retention add-on. Happy to walk through this on a quick call — suggest Tue, Nov 23 at 10am PT if that works for you.

Best,
Neha
